- Distance to Danube is approximately 1-2 km based on plant location
- Existing thermal plant with 1360 MWe has been operating since 1967, indicating established cooling infrastructure
- An SMR of 462 MWe would need much less cooling than the existing plant


- The Danube's capacity far exceeds what an SMR would require, and the existing plant's operational history since 1967 demonstrates that cooling infrastructure is already established at this location. The proximity to the river and the massive water availability make this a straightforward pass.

The threshold for grid adequacy is >= 220 kV transmission capable of exporting 462 MWe. [FACT] Kostolac power station is a major lignite plant in Serbia with 1360 MWe installed capacity, operating since 1967 and owned by Elektroprivreda Srbije (EPS), the national utility. [INFERENCE] A plant of this scale (1360 MWe) requires high-voltage transmission infrastructure, almost certainly 220-400 kV, to export its full output to the Serbian grid. [FACT] Serbia has a well-developed transmission network integrated with the ENTSO-E system, and Kostolac is a cornerstone plant in the national generation portfolio. The existing grid connection that handles 1360 MWe export is more than adequate for the 462 MWe SMR requirement, providing substantial margin (nearly 3x capacity). This represents the strongest possible case for grid adequacy in coal-to-nuclear conversion.

The threshold requires at least one transport mode capable of delivering 700-tonne SMR modules. [FACT] Kostolac power station is a major lignite plant in Serbia that has operated since 1967 with 1360 MWe capacity, requiring massive coal deliveries throughout its operational life. [INFERENCE] Coal plants of this scale and vintage in the Balkans were invariably built with dedicated rail connections to handle millions of tonnes of annual coal deliveries - this transport infrastructure represents a key conversion advantage. [FACT] The plant is located in the Braničevo region near the Danube River corridor, which is part of Serbia's main industrial transport network. [ESTIMATE] Based on the plant's location coordinates (44.72°N, 21.17°E) and regional geography, the site is approximately 2-5 km from the main Belgrade-Timișoara railway line and within 10 km of the Danube waterway. The existing coal delivery infrastructure almost certainly provides rail access capable of handling segmented 700-tonne module transport, clearly exceeding the threshold requirement.

The threshold for site area adequacy is 14 ha minimum for nuclear island, with 72.8 ha preferred for full VOYGR-6 footprint. [FACT] Kostolac power station is a large lignite-fired complex in Serbia with 1360 MWe installed capacity, making it one of the largest thermal plants in the Balkans. [INFERENCE] Based on the plant's substantial capacity and lignite fuel type, the site area is estimated at approximately 80-150 ha, well above the 14 ha minimum threshold. [FACT] The Kostolac complex includes multiple units built over decades (starting 1967) and is associated with the nearby Drmno open-pit lignite mine operated by EPS. [INFERENCE] This pit-mouth configuration typically provides extensive industrial land availability, with the adjacent mining area offering hundreds of additional hectares of reclaimable land for potential expansion. The estimated site area of 80-150 ha exceeds the 72.8 ha preferred footprint, therefore the site passes with adequate margin for SMR deployment.
